messages:
sam_onboard: Heads up — the sample in our "quickstart/next-edge" still uses require(). Deploying to Vercel edge errors with "Cannot use import statement outside a module". Local node (server) works fine. Anyone seen this?

nina_sdk: Yep, edge = ESM only. We ship both entry points but the example accidentally shows the CJS style. For edge users we should show an ESM example and a TypeScript configuration snippet.

harmon_build: Reproduced on our CI mirror. The failing log shows static require import at top level causing the runtime to treat file as CJS. Quick mitigation is to switch to named ESM imports or dynamic import inside the handler.

sam_onboard: Example from docs that breaks:
```js
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
```
This explodes on deploy.

nina_sdk: Recommended ESM variant (preferred for TS + edge):
```ts
import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference';
const client = createClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
export default async function handler(req) { /* ... */ }
```
Note: prefer named import for better type inference. Default export is provided for CJS ergonomics but can become `any` in some TS configs.

zoe_docs: Good catch. I'll update the quickstart to show the ESM snippet first, then a dynamic-import fallback for consumers who can't switch their whole project yet. I'll also add a tiny TS section: set "module": "esnext" and "moduleResolution": "node16" or "nodeNext" and mention esModuleInterop caveats.

harmon_build: Also flag for bundlers: pastes from webpack/next can rewrite ESM to CJS depending on target. For edge builds ensure the bundler outputs ESM (Next config: experimental.outputFileTracingRoot / target: 'experimental-serverless-trace' is unrelated — the important bit is module output). Might be worth adding a one-line note.

sam_onboard: One additional gotcha I hit: when using `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` my editor showed poor autocomplete. Switching to `import { createClient }` fixed it. Can we call that out so users who rely on typings are steered toward named import?

nina_sdk: Agreed. SDK side note: we publish both, but default export is effectively a compat layer. We'll update type declarations so default export has better typing where possible, but docs should recommend named imports for TS.

ci-bot: Integration test failed: examples/next-edge (edge-runner) — exit 1. See https://ci.internal/redwood/4902 for logs.

zoe_docs: I'll open a PR to fix the sample and add the TS/bundler troubleshooting block. PR link will be posted here; will include a test update to run the example in an edge-like environment in CI.

harmon_build: Once PR merges let's also add a lint rule to detect top-level require in /examples/next-edge so we don't regress. Small CI job could run node --experimental-vm-modules to validate ESM import shape.

sam_onboard: Awesome, please tag me on the PR — I'll validate on Vercel preview. Thanks!
